title: Standardize pricing experiment readout visualizations (cohorts, confidence, margin overlays)
creator: Chris Osei
description:
Context
We have multiple Q1 pricing/packaging experiments running and we need consistent, defensible readouts for (a) exec decisions and (b) AE/SE enablement materials. Current charts are inconsistent across decks and don’t reliably communicate cohort definitions, confidence, and gross margin impact. We also need a standard way to annotate when meter changes overlap with experiment windows (pre/post segmentation) so we don’t oversell conclusions.

This ticket defines the “standard experiment readout visualization kit” used in:
- Exec update: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/company/executive-update-pricing-and-metering-feb-2026.json
- Sales readout draft deck: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/pricing-experiment-readout-slide-draft.json
- Confluence pricing guidance pages (via screenshots / exports)

Goals
1) Standard chart templates for experiment readouts:
   - Conversion (activation) lift
   - Retention / repeat usage
   - ARPU / net revenue per account
   - Gross margin overlay and/or cost-to-serve overlays
   - Plan mix / packaging movement (e.g., free → paid → committed)

2) Standard cohort + caveat framing built into the visual system:
   - Cohort summary chip (eligibility, timeframe, exclusions)
   - Metering caveat / “meter version” badge (pre/post fix)
   - Confidence & sample size callouts (where applicable)

3) Fast-to-produce exports that work in:
   - Slides (Google Slides)
   - Confluence pages
   - Optional: Redwood Console internal dashboards screenshots (stylistic alignment, not pixel-perfect)

Non-goals
- Designing new pricing pages / public marketing pages
- Replacing analytics source-of-truth dashboards
- Defining metric definitions (owned by PM/Finance: PM-1848)

Proposed visualization kit (v1)
A) Readout header block (always included)
- Experiment name + variant summary
- Dates (start/end) + rollout status
- Cohort definition chip(s): “New self-serve”, “Existing paid”, “Sales-led excluded”, “EU-only”, etc.
- Data health badges:
  - “Meter version: tokens_v2” / “pre-fix tokens_v1”
  - “Freshness: T+N hrs” (optional, for internal only)
- Links (small) to cohort doc + analysis plan

B) Primary KPI tiles (1 slide / page)
- 3–5 tiles max with consistent structure:
  - Metric name
  - Control value
  - Variant value
  - Delta (absolute + relative)
  - N (accounts) and/or N (requests) depending on metric
  - Confidence indicator (see section E)

C) Lift over time line chart (for conversion/activation)
- X: time (day or week)
- Y: conversion rate (or activation rate)
- Two lines: Control vs Variant
- Shaded “meter change window” overlay if applicable (light vertical band)
- Annotations for rollout steps (flag ramp)
- Footer with exclusions and known confounders (max 2 lines)

D) Margin overlay chart (exec-required)
Option 1 (preferred): Dual-axis with clear labeling and de-emphasis of secondary axis
- Bars: net revenue / account (or ARPU)
- Line: gross margin % (or cost per 1K tokens)
- Grouped by: control/variant, optionally split by “model mix bucket”

Option 2: Waterfall (when packaging changes shift multiple levers)
- Start: baseline gross margin
- Steps: change in revenue rate, change in cache-hit, change in model mix, change in retries/idempotency, etc.
- End: net margin

E) Confidence visualization rules (align with Sana + FP&A)
- Always show N and time window.
- If we have proper statistical treatment, show 90%/95% CI:
  - Use error bars on delta-only charts.
  - Avoid clutter on time series; use a small “CI available” tag + show CI on delta summary.
- If we do not have reliable CI (e.g., heavily confounded), show “Directional” tag and require a caveat note.

F) Cohort segmentation small multiples (when needed)
- Up to 4 panels:
  - New vs existing
  - Self-serve vs sales-led (if included)
  - High volume vs low volume
  - US vs EU (only if region pricing differs)
- Rule: if a segmentation panel flips the conclusion, it must be called out explicitly in the “Decision” slide.

Visual language / style guidelines
- Use Redwood internal deck style (neutral backgrounds, high contrast text).
- Control = graphite/gray; Variant = Redwood green/teal (avoid “warning red” unless negative outcome specifically called out).
- Use one consistent delta color treatment:
  - Positive = green
  - Negative = red
  - Neutral/noise = gray
- Meter caveat badge should be visually distinct from confidence badge to prevent conflation.
- Margin overlays must label axes clearly and use subtle gridlines.

Accessibility
- Color contrast must pass for text and key plot elements.
- Do not rely on color alone for control vs variant (use line styles or point shapes).

Deliverables
1) Figma file with:
- Component library (tiles, header chips, badges)
- Chart templates (time series, delta bars w/ CI, dual-axis margin overlay, waterfall)
- Example slide layouts (Exec summary slide, Detailed KPI slide, Caveats/Decision slide)

2) “How to use” one-pager for PM/Ops (exporting charts for slides and when to choose each chart type)

3) Exportable slide assets (SVG/PNG) + layout guidance

Acceptance criteria
- Chris (Product Ops) can drop templates into the readout deck with minimal manual formatting (<30 min per experiment section).
- Sana signs off that confidence display matches analysis approach (or “Directional” is enforced where CI is not valid).
- Rishi signs off that margin overlay is readable and not misleading.
- Jordan/Sales enablement confirms the charts are legible in a customer-facing context (no internal-only badges in AE-facing version).

Open questions
- Do we standardize on 90% or 95% CI for exec readouts (or make it configurable)? Pending: Sana.
- Should the “meter version” badge be shown in AE materials, or only in internal exec readouts? Proposed: internal only, unless directly relevant to a customer dispute.
- What’s the canonical naming for meter versions (tokens_v1/v2 vs “pre/post retry fix”)? Pending: Telemetry (Logan/Nadia) + PM-1842.

Links / references
- Analysis plan: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/product-ops/pricing-experiment-analysis-plan-2026q1.json
- Cohort definitions: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/hosted-api/experiment-vs-control-cohort-definitions.json
- Slide draft: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/pricing-experiment-readout-slide-draft.json
- Meter overlap caveat thread (for context): sources/slack/product/1770243102-experiment-caveat-meter-change-overlap.json

Latest updates
2026-02-12 (Soojin)
- Drafted v1 header block + KPI tiles in Figma. Added separate badges for “Confidence” and “Meter version”.
- Decision: Control/Variant colors locked (graphite vs teal). Avoid using red/green except for delta annotations.

2026-02-18 (Sana Farid comment)
- Strong preference to not show CI on time series; show CI only on the delta summary chart + require N.
- Use “Directional” tag when we don’t meet minimum sample thresholds; do not imply statistical significance.

2026-02-20 (Rishi Malhotra comment)
- Margin overlay must support showing both gross margin % and cost per 1K tokens for internal readers. Suggest dual templates.
- Add explicit label for “includes credits/discounts?” so Finance doesn’t have to re-litigate in every deck.

2026-02-24 (Jordan Blake comment)
- For AE-facing version, remove anything that reads like we’re uncertain about billing integrity unless the story is explicitly about metering fixes.
- Keep the cohort summary chip (helps objection handling: “Who is this true for?”).

Next steps
- Incorporate feedback and publish the template pack to the shared drive for Product Ops + Sales Enablement.
- Coordinate with DES-712 to align dashboard layout tiles with these templates (terminology + colors).
- Confirm final confidence rules once PM-1848 is done; update template copy accordingly.

Comments
- Chris Osei (2026-02-09): Please ensure templates accommodate the pre/post meter fix segmentation requirement. We’re going to have at least one experiment where the meter fix lands mid-window.
- Nadia Rahman (2026-02-21): Suggest using “meter revision” language rather than “fix” to avoid implying prior billing was wrong. Happy to provide canonical revision labels once ENG-4430/PR-27463 rollout is complete.
- Evelyn Hart (2026-02-25): For exec readout, I want a single “Decision slide” layout that forces: recommendation, expected impact range, and top 3 risks/caveats. Can we add that to deliverables v1?

Definition of done
- Figma templates complete + shared
- Example slides exported and placed in the readout deck draft
- Stakeholder approvals recorded (Product Ops + Finance + Sales enablement)
- Follow-up ticket created if we need a v2 iteration for additional chart types (e.g., survivorship curves, payback period)
